question: Should employers be barred from firing staff over lawful opinions they post in their own time?
answer: Yes. Few people can afford to lose a job over a clumsy post, and that fear silences far more than are ever fired. Some places already protect it: California bars employers from controlling workers' political activity, and Connecticut protects employee speech unless it disrupts the work. A livelihood is too high a price.
move: Whichever side you took, the line between opinion and conduct decides it.
ask: Would I want my job to depend on the worst thing I ever posted?
counterpoint: No. Staff are a firm's public face; one viral post can drive off customers, upset colleagues and make others feel unsafe at work. Narrow rules already cover harassment and disruption, but a broad ban would make courts decide what counts as an opinion. A firm forced to keep someone who insulted its own clients is not free either.
